transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-21
- Time: 14:30 - 15:28 UTC (58m)
- Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Dr Priya Raman, Marcus Lee, Sara O'Neill, Tom Winters (procurement joined ~10m in)

Summary: quick intro, Helios overview of clinical summarization use case (PHI), traffic / tokens estimate, strict residency and HIPAA requirement, explore hosted pilot then Dedicated or Private based on BAA and unit economics. Discussed per-token pricing levers (batching, prefix/KV caching), quantization, and tradeoffs on latency vs cost. Agreed Redwood will send security docs and run a unit-econ model with Helios sample traffic.

Topics covered:
- Use case: discharge summary generation + coding assistance (clinical notes, average length ~700-900 tokens)
- Traffic profile: near-term 2M tokens/day, growth scenarios 6M tokens/day
- Latency SLO: 400-800ms P50 for request path (clinician-facing)
- Privacy/residency: PHI, need BAA, VPC or on-prem path considered
- Cost controls: batching windows, prefix/KV cache, model quantization, routing to cheaper variants for non-critical workloads
- Pilot scope and commercial path: hosted pilot → dedicated reserved pool or Private (VPC/on-prem) depending on security & cost

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about, about an hour. Quick round — could you each intro?
[00:08] Dr. Priya Raman: Sure, Im Priya, I head AI at Helios, were building a clinical summarization pipeline to generate discharge summaries and coding suggestions, we have PHI so HIPAA is non-negotiable.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Marcus, platform eng, Ill be hands on for infra and pilot stuff. We want clarity on where data lives and key mgmt.
[00:28] Sara O'Neill: Sara, cloud ops, I manage cloud security and compliance for the AI team.
[00:33] Avery: Great, and Im Avery from Redwood, AE, with Diego whos our solutions engineer focusing on performance and cost.
[00:40] Diego: Hey all.
[00:47] Tom Winters (Speaker 1): Tom here, procurement quick note, budget cycle question later.

[01:02] Dr. Priya Raman: Our immediate ask: wed like to run a pilot to validate quality and cost. Typical note size average is ~800 tokens, peak concurrent clinicians maybe 30–40. Overall were estimating around 2 million tokens a day to start.
[01:28] Avery: Perfect, thats a nice starting point. Two million tokens/day maps to different unit economics depending on whether you use Hosted or Dedicated. For hosted we bill per token with our published rates; Dedicated gets you a reserved GPU pool which drops unit cost if you commit.
[01:49] Marcus Lee: Can you quantify "drops"? Were trying to hit a $25k / month budget if possible — thats a soft cap.
[01:58] Diego: Right, so ballpark — with hosted and no batching your per-token end cost is higher; with batching and prefix caching you can reduce effective tokens by 20–40% for repeat system prompts and shared context. With Dedicated, if you commit to a monthly capacity you typically see another 25–40% reduction versus on-demand hosted in our models, depends on utilization.
[02:25] Dr. Priya Raman: Important quirk — most of the context is PHI. Are you caching patient context? Thats a no-go without strong encryption and customer KMS.
[02:38] Avery: Absolutely. For PHI we recommend either a Private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed key support. We support KV/prefix caching but customers can opt out or have the cache encrypted with customer KMS, and the cache can be pinned to a VPC or even on-prem.
[02:58] Sara O'Neill: Is the cache persisted? How long? We need auditability and TTL controls.
[03:07] Diego: TTL is configurable; eviction policies also. And everything is logged — audit logs show read/write events and we can tie them to request IDs. Wed provide audit log exports for compliance. Note: transcription here might say "KeV cache" sometimes, but we mean KV cache or prefix cache.
[03:27] Marcus Lee: If we do prefix caching for templates (non-PHI parts) and keep PHI out, maybe we can get most of the benefits.
[03:35] Dr. Priya Raman: Yes we could split: de-identify before caching. But de-id step adds latency; is that reasonable?
[03:44] Diego: You can run de-id upstream in your pipeline, yes; that adds processing but if you batch de-id with batching windows of 50–200ms you can still meet a 400–800ms SLO. Batching reduces per-token GPU overhead by combining requests.
[04:02] Avery: On quantization — we support 4-bit quantization profiles for many open models which reduces cost and memory; tradeoff is small quality delta. For clinical text we recommend validating on your evals; many customers do a quick A/B to check coding accuracy.
[04:18] Dr. Priya Raman: How about latency with quantized models?
[04:22] Diego: Often similar or slightly faster due to smaller memory traffic on the GPU; depends on model shape and kernel selection. For strict P50 400ms wed run benchmarks with your note length distribution.
[04:34] Sara O'Neill: Residency — PHI must remain in our AWS region, we cant route outside. Do you support region pinning for hosted?
[04:42] Avery: Yes, we offer region pins on hosted for enterprise tiers; Dedicated gives you explicit capacity in a region, and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC or on-prem.
[04:54] Tom Winters: Question on contractual stuff — we need a BAA and SOC2 evidence to consider hosted for PHI.
[05:01] Avery: We will share the BAA + SOC2/ISO pack after this call — action item.
[05:06] Dr. Priya Raman: Back to unit economics — can you run a concrete example: 2M tokens/day, 800 token average per request, 30 average concurrent clinical flows, target cost < $25k/month?
[05:20] Diego: Sure, quick calc: 2M tokens/day is ~60M tokens/month. If hosted per-token rate (example) is $0.0002/token thats $12k/month raw, but thats simplified because system prompts and repeated context increase counted tokens. With no batching and no cache that could be 30–50% higher. If you add batching/caching and run on a quantized model you could get effective token burn down. Dedicated with a monthly commit might reduce unit price to $0.00012/token equivalent — ballpark — getting you into your budget zone. Well run real numbers in the spreadsheet.
[06:03] Marcus Lee: Those per-token numbers vary a lot — I want to see a model with sensitivity: hosted on-demand, hosted with batching, dedicated medium commit, dedicated high commit, private on-prem cost buckets.
[06:15] Avery: Yep well produce that. We usually deliver a populated spreadsheet that shows token burn, compute hours, amortized GPU cost, and network/ops adders.
[06:26] Dr. Priya Raman: What about fallback policies? If Dedicated capacity saturates, can we fallback to cheaper hosted variants? We need graceful degradation, not errors.
[06:36] Diego: We have smart routing — you can configure fallbacks to compatible model variants in other regions or hosted capacity. You can also set latency or cost thresholds to choose cheaper variants for background jobs.
[06:48] Sara O'Neill: For audit & keys: can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS/HSM and the key never leaves our account?
[06:56] Avery: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Dedicated and Private and for hosted with enterprise options — the key can be in your account and we access via cross-account role under strict controls; we can detail in the security packet.
[07:08] Marcus Lee: Perf test — wed like Redwood to run a P50/P95 test with our note distribution on an H100-backed instance and a quantized profile.
[07:17] Diego: We can run that in the pilot. For the hosted pilot we spin up an isolated org instance in the target region and run the benchmarks with a sample set you provide. If you want on-prem tests thats also possible but requires more lead time.
[07:32] Dr. Priya Raman: Pilot timeline — wed like a 2-week hosted pilot, validate quality, cost, perf, and then decide commit. Procurement wants pricing options for Dedicated reserve vs hosted burn estimate.
[07:43] Tom Winters: Right, procurement will want a few commitment tiers and a PO template.
[07:49] Avery: Noted. Well send the pricing tiers and a PO template.
[07:55] Marcus Lee: About caching: If we de-id and cache templates, do you provide tools or do we handle de-id?
[08:02] Diego: Typically customers do de-id upstream in their pipeline and only send de-id tokens to the cache. We provide SDKs and examples for that pattern. If you want we can include a sample lambda transform in the pilot repo.
[08:14] Dr. Priya Raman: One more — how do you measure "effective tokens saved" with caching? We need a clear metric to report back to execs.
[08:22] Diego: We provide token-level telemetry — you can see raw tokens in requests vs effective billed tokens after cache hits and dedup. We produce a dashboard with percent cache hit and effective token burn.
[08:34] Sara O'Neill: Any regulatory issues around caching de-identified content? We need legal to sign off.
[08:40] Avery: Thats reasonable. Well include legal notes in the security packet and you can run a brief legal review during the pilot.
[08:50] Dr. Priya Raman: Ok, decision criteria: 1) meet accuracy for coding and summaries, 2) cost under or near $25k/month at projected volume, 3) BAA and audit controls validated.
[09:04] Avery: Great — next steps: we send BAA & security docs by Thursday, Diego will run the spreadsheet with your sample numbers and return a populated econ model, and we schedule the pilot kickoff for early Jan (assuming access is provisioned).
[09:20] Tom Winters: Can you get procurement pricing options in the same packet?
[09:24] Avery: Yes, well include tiered commit options and PO templates.
[09:29] Marcus Lee: Ill upload a sanitized sample set tonight for benchmarking.
[09:33] Dr. Priya Raman: Ill have legal review priority once we get the BAA.
[09:37] Avery: Awesome. Anything else?
[09:40] Sara O'Neill: One quick nit — are there tokenization differences between models we should account for? Sometimes the same payload tokenizes differently on different model families.
[09:49] Diego: Yep good point. We account for tokenizer differences in the model profiles and the spreadsheet. We recommend measuring actual token counts using the target model family in the pilot.
[09:59] Dr. Priya Raman: Thanks everyone.
[10:02] Avery: Thanks, well follow up with the packet and the econ model.

End of transcript.
